deep.reconstruction:
Context: §2 'Produits tensoriels hilbertiens. Applications à des inégalités diverses' of Grothendieck's 1953 functional-analysis notes. The previous page defines the Hilbert tensor product of Hilbert spaces E_1,...,E_n: the product scalar on decomposable tensors is (a_1⊗…⊗a_n, b_1⊗…⊗b_n) = Π(a_i,b_i), and the completion is written ⊗̂^{(2)}E_i. It then states inequality (2): ||u_1⊗…⊗u_n|| ≤ Π||u_i|| for bounded u_i: E_i→F_i.

This page gives the proof of (2).
(i) Factor u_1⊗…⊗u_n = U_1∘…∘U_n, where each U_i is a tensor product of identities and the single operator u_i. So it suffices to treat the case where all factors but one are the identity.
(ii) A crossed-out attempt uses orthonormal bases: E_i ≅ ℓ²(A_i), F_i ≅ ℓ²(B_i), and ⊗^{(2)}E_i ≅ ℓ²(A_1×…×A_n).
(iii) The kept argument uses associativity and commutativity of the Hilbert tensor product to reduce to two factors: E_1 and E_2, F_1 and F_2 = E_2, with A_1 ∈ L(E_1,F_1) and A_2 = 1.
(iv) Identify E_1⊗^{(2)}E_2 with the Hilbert–Schmidt operators L^{(2)}(\bar E_1', E_2), and likewise F_1⊗^{(2)}E_2 with L^{(2)}(\bar F_1', E_2). Under this identification A_1⊗1 becomes u ↦ u∘ᵗA_1.
(v) The claim is then the ideal inequality ||u ᵗA_1||_2 ≤ ||u||_2 ||ᵗA_1|| for Hilbert–Schmidt operators, which is formula (17) of No 1.
(vi) Consequently ⊗u_i extends by continuity to a bounded map ⊗̂^{(2)}E_i → ⊗̂^{(2)}F_i, denoted the same way.
(vii) He then starts the next construction: on ⊗̂^{n(2)}E, set (3) a_n = (1/n!) Σ_{σ∈S_n} ε_σ σ, with σ acting as the symmetry operators. The next page shows a_n is an orthogonal projector. It defines the Hilbert exterior power Λ̂^{(n)}E as the range of a_n with the inner product scaled by n!, and derives (a_1∧…∧a_n, b_1∧…∧b_n) = det((a_i,b_j)).

Purpose: to set up Hilbert tensor and exterior powers, with norm estimates for ⊗u_i and Λ^n u. These are the tools used for determinant and Fredholm-type inequalities ('inégalités diverses'), as in Grothendieck's Fredholm-theory work.
errors: No mathematical error. Notation drifts from u_i to A_i in the middle of the proof. In the factorisation U_1∘…∘U_n the intermediate spaces (F_1⊗…⊗F_{i-1}⊗E_i⊗…⊗E_n) are not specified, but the intent is clear.

The two-factor reduction quietly uses that the identification with L^{(2)}(\bar E_1',E_2) carries A_1⊗1 to right composition with the transpose of A_1 (conjugate-linear dual conventions). This is correct but left implicit.

ideas.what: Norm inequality ||⊗u_i|| ≤ Π||u_i|| on Hilbert tensor products, proved by reduction to one non-identity factor and to the Hilbert–Schmidt ideal inequality
ideas.modern_name: Cross-norm / functoriality of the Hilbert space tensor product; Hilbert–Schmidt ideal property
ideas.where_published: Produits tensoriels topologiques et espaces nucléaires (Memoirs AMS 1955) treats Hilbert tensor products / Hilbert–Schmidt identification; also La théorie de Fredholm (Bull. SMF 1956)

ideas.what: Identification of E_1⊗̂^{(2)}E_2 with Hilbert–Schmidt operators from the conjugate dual of E_1 to E_2
Antisymmetrisation projector a_n and Hilbert exterior power with determinant inner product
ideas.modern_name: Fermionic Fock space component / Hilbert exterior power Λ^n H
ideas.where_published: La théorie de Fredholm (Bull. SMF 84, 1956) uses exterior powers of Hilbert/Banach spaces for determinant estimates

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but entirely standard textbook proof of the boundedness of tensor products of operators on Hilbert tensor products, followed by the start of the antisymmetrizer construction. It is a draft of material Grothendieck used in his published 1955–56 work; nothing on the page is new.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out first line likely reads '... de [vérifier?] ... u_1⊗ ... ⊗u_n'; the kept line is 'on a u_1⊗…⊗u_n = U_1∘…∘U_n, où U_i est le produit tensoriel des opérateurs, l'un égal à l'identité ..., [le i-ème] égal à u_i'.
The ℓ²(A_i), ℓ²(B_1), ℓ²(A_1×…×A_n) passage sits inside a boxed and struck-through region with connecting curves. It appears to be an abandoned basis-based proof, not part of the final text.
The reference after the Hilbert–Schmidt inequality reads '(17), du No 1', followed by 'voir aussi (3)' or similar. The '(3)' is not the formula (3) defining a_n further down.
The bottom line reads 'les ... du deuxième membre sont considérés comme les opérateurs de symétrie dans ⊗̂^{n(2)}E (ε_σ signature de la permutation σ)'.
